title: Marswalk science stops
description: Text, Perseverance images and a sampling checklist for the two science stops. Each stop links to a route.json waypoint by name. Every sentence and image carries the shared provenance block from public/data/README.md. Shown in Plan mode when a waypoint is selected and in Walk mode on arrival (card: #66).
frame: x east, z south, metres from Cheyava Falls (engine frame, same as route.json)

tags.DATA: Measured or reported by a NASA mission, a NASA release or a peer-reviewed paper. The provenance block names the source and quotes it.
tags.DERIVED: Calculated by us from DATA values. The note gives the calculation.
tags.SIM: Our own assumption or game choice. The note says why and what it is based on.

image_credit_rule: Show the credit string next to every image, always.

stops.summary: The rock with "leopard spots" that NASA called a potential biosignature in 2025. Perseverance cored it on 21 July 2024.

text.sentence: Cheyava Falls is an arrowhead-shaped rock, 1 m by 0.6 m, that Perseverance found in the Bright Angel formation in July 2024.

provenance.site: Bright Angel formation, Neretva Vallis, Jezero crater
provenance.reference: NASA news release, "NASA Says Mars Rover Discovered Potential Biosignature Last Year", 10 September 2025
provenance.locator: "Perseverance came upon Cheyava Falls in July 2024 while exploring the “Bright Angel” formation" and "an arrowhead-shaped rock measuring 3.2 feet by 2 feet (1 meter by 0.6 meters)"
provenance.license: NASA material, not copyrighted in the United States; credit NASA/JPL-Caltech as stated (NASA media usage guidelines, https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/)
provenance.note: Historical observation, not a current condition.

text.sentence: It holds organic compounds, white calcium sulfate veins and millimetre-size "leopard spots" whose black rims contain iron and phosphate.

provenance.reference: NASA/JPL news release, "NASA's Perseverance Rover Scientists Find Intriguing Mars Rock", 25 July 2024

provenance.license: NASA material, not copyrighted in the United States; credit NASA/JPL-Caltech as stated (NASA media usage guidelines, https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/)

text.sentence: In September 2025 the team reported in Nature that the spots likely hold vivianite and greigite, iron minerals that microbes can make but that also form without life, so NASA calls them a potential biosignature.

provenance.reference: Marswalk outcrop mask public/marswalk/assets/outcrop_mask.jpg (from the HiRISE orthomosaic); issue #265
provenance.locator: The position note of this stop: light-toned over the whole 8 m around the point
provenance.license: Project text, same license as the repository
provenance.note: Built from the position note. The brightness is HiRISE data; reading it as rock like Bright Angel’s is our assumption, and no rover image of this spot exists, so the line is SIM.

provenance.site: Neretva Vallis, Jezero crater, next to the Marswalk habitat
provenance.reference: Issue #265 (short first mission); Marswalk terrain tile public/marswalk/assets/terrain.json and outcrop mask public/marswalk/assets/outcrop_mask.jpg, both from HiRISE
provenance.locator: Chosen with src/sim/routePlanner.js on the cost grid from the airlock entry of public/data/shelters.json (535.1, 574.1)
provenance.license: Project text, same license as the repository
provenance.note: Our choice of point for the first sortie. It is 55 m of walking from the airlock, about 2 min out and back at 1 m/s: the planner route is the straight line (54.8 m), on ground no steeper than 12.7 deg, 2.9 m lower than the airlock. The spot itself slopes 3.3 deg. The HiRISE outcrop mask is light-toned over the whole 8 m around it (the brightness the Outcrop layer shows), the kind of rock Bright Angel is made of, but no rover has looked at this spot: the science is an assumption. It lies 13 deg off the heading the airlock faces, so the stop is ahead of the crew as they step out, and the habitat mast is in sight.

provenance.site: Neretva Vallis, Jezero crater, next to the Marswalk habitat
provenance.reference: Issue #61 (arrival radius) and issue #265 (short first mission); outcrop mask public/marswalk/assets/outcrop_mask.jpg, from HiRISE
provenance.locator: Issue #61: "2 m at a science target, 5 m elsewhere"; the light-toned ground around the point in the outcrop mask
provenance.license: Project text, same license as the repository
provenance.note: Our choice. The stop is a patch of light-toned ground, not one rock: the outcrop mask is light-toned over the whole 8 m around the point, and a sample anywhere on it is a sample of the patch. So reaching the patch counts as reaching the stop, where a science target that is one rock uses 2 m (issue #61).
